 Oral Judgment
(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vijaykumar A.Patil)
1.

This appeal is by the claimants seeking for higher compensation being aggrieved by the judgment
and award dated 23.04.2018, passed in Mvc No.158/2015 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge &
Mact, Kushtagi.

2. Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that on 06.09.2012, the deceased was moving on his
motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-29/Q-0403, at that time, he met with an accident and
sustained grievous injuries and later he succumbed to those injuries.

It is averred that, the deceased
was Doctor by profession and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

The claim petition is filed by the
mother and brother of the deceased.

3. The respondents entered appearance, opposed the claim petition by denying the age, income and
avocation of the deceased and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

Learned counsel Shri A.B. Patil appearing for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has
committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month and he seeks
to assess the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month.

Thus, he seeks to reassess the entire
compensation as per law by allowing the appeal.

5. Per contra, learned counsel Shri Suresh S.Gundi appearing for respondent No.2 supports the
impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submits that no evidence is placed on
record with regard to the income and avocation of the deceased.

He further submits that the
Tribunal has justified in awarding the total compensation of Rs.8,68,000/- with 8% interest.

Thus,
he seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

6. We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the parties and meticulously
perused the materials available on record.

7.

It is not in dispute that the son of claimant No.1 was proceedings on a motorcycle on 06.09.2012,
met with accident, sustained grievous injuries and later he succumbed to those injuries.

The
evidence available on records shows that the deceased was aged about 30 years at the time of
accident and was a Doctor by profession (Rmp Doctor).

Taking note of his avocation and age, we are
of the considered view that it would be just and proper to reassess the income of the deceased at
Rs.13,000/- per month.

The claimants are entitled to the addition of 40% of the assessed income
under the head of loss of future prospects.

Since, the deceased was a bachelor, 50% of the assessed
income needs to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

Thus, the
claimants are entitled to compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' would be Rs.17,47,200/-
(Rs.13,000/- + 40% - 50% x 12 x 16).

8. The appellants-claimants would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of estate'
and Nc: 2024:Khc-D:11629-Db Rs.15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses & transportation of dead
body' with 10% escalation.

Further, the appellants- claimants would be entitled to a sum of
Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of consortium' with 10% escalation.

9. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:
1. Towards Loss of dependency Rs.17,47,200/- (Rs.13,000/- + 40% - 50% x 12 x 16)
2 . Towards loss of estate Rs.16,500/- (Rs.15,000/- + 10%)

3. Towards funeral expenses & Rs.16,500/-
transportation of dead body (Rs.15,000/- + 10%)
4. Towards loss of consortium Rs.88,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- x 2 + 10%) Total Rs.18,68,200/-
10.

In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
Order
(i) The appeal stands partly allowed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the
appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.18,68,200/- as aga
inst Rs.8,68,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11629-DB (iii) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
